title: Implement load_rgb for HEIC, JPG, and PNG
description: Create `src/lumamatch/io_image.py` with a single loader that returns a plain uint8 RGB array from any supported file, normalizing away the format differences (palette, grayscale, alpha, EXIF orientation) so the rest of the pipeline never has to think about them.
acceptanceCriteria: `load_rgb(path) -> np.ndarray` returns uint8 with shape (H, W, 3) for .heic, .heif, .jpg, .jpeg, and .png inputs
`pillow_heif.register_heif_opener()` is called exactly once at module import
Grayscale ('L') input is expanded to 3 identical channels
RGBA/LA input has alpha dropped (not composited) and returns 3 channels
Palette ('P') input is converted to RGB
EXIF orientation is applied via `ImageOps.exif_transpose` so a rotated JPEG loads upright
An unsupported extension raises `ValueError` naming the extension and listing supported ones
A missing file raises `FileNotFoundError` with the path in the message
A corrupt/undecodable file raises `ValueError` wrapping the underlying error rather than leaking a PIL exception type
`SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS` is a module-level frozenset used by both the loader and the CLI
Unit tests cover every mode above; `ruff check` clean

steps.details: Import `numpy`, `Path`, `Image`, `ImageOps`, `UnidentifiedImageError` from PIL, and `pillow_heif`. Call `pillow_heif.register_heif_opener()` at module level with a comment explaining it must happen before any `.heic` open. Define `SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS = frozenset({'.heic', '.heif', '.jpg', '.jpeg', '.png'})`.

Write `_validate_source(path) -> Path`: coerce to `Path`, expanduser, resolve. If suffix.lower() not in SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS raise `ValueError(f"unsupported image format '{suffix}'; supported: ...")` with the extensions sorted. If not `path.is_file()` raise `FileNotFoundError(str(path))`.

Open with `Image.open(path)` inside a `with` block. Wrap in try/except catching `UnidentifiedImageError` and `OSError`, re-raising as `ValueError(f'could not decode {path}: {exc}')`. Apply `ImageOps.exif_transpose(img)`. Then if `img.mode != 'RGB'`, call `img.convert('RGB')` — this handles L, LA, P, RGBA, and CMYK in one step and drops alpha without compositing.
Return `np.asarray(img, dtype=np.uint8)`. Assert (with a raised ValueError, not `assert`) that the result has ndim 3 and shape[2] == 3, to catch any surprising mode conversion.

steps.description: Write unit tests with generated fixtures
steps.details: Create `tests/test_io_load.py`. Use `tmp_path` to write test files with Pillow: an RGB PNG, an RGB JPEG, an RGB HEIC, an 'L' PNG, an 'RGBA' PNG, and a 'P' PNG. For each, assert the loaded shape is (H,W,3) and dtype uint8. For the 'L' case assert all three channels are equal. For RGBA assert shape[2] == 3.
Assert `ValueError` for a `.bmp` path, `FileNotFoundError` for a nonexistent `.png`, and `ValueError` for a `.png` file containing random bytes (write `b'not an image'` to it).
Run `.venv/bin/pytest tests/ -q` and `.venv/bin/ruff check src tests`.

technicalNotes: Dropping alpha rather than compositing onto white is deliberate: compositing would alter L* of transparent regions and silently change the histogram. Document this in the README (TASK-26).
`ImageOps.exif_transpose` returns a new image and may return None on some Pillow versions if there is no EXIF — guard with `img = ImageOps.exif_transpose(img) or img`.
`img.convert('RGB')` on a CMYK JPEG works but the result is approximate; CMYK is not a supported input per the PRD, so it is acceptable that it silently converts.
Do not raise Pillow's MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS limit — TASK-25 depends on it staying at the default.
